stops.name: Melk Abbey
stops.quote: Cultural highlights like castle ruins, Melk Abbey , and villages like Dürnstein and Weißenkirchen add to the area's calm, timeless appeal.

stops.name: Melk
stops.quote: Notable places in the Wachau include: Melk : Known for the baroque Melk Abbey, one of Europe’s most impressive monastic buildings.

stops.name: Spitz an der Donau
stops.quote: Spitz an der Donau : A charming wine village, famous for the Tausendeimerberg, a steeply terraced vineyard.

stops.name: 1000-Eimerberg
stops.quote: White wines thrive here, particularly on hillsides like the 1000-Eimerberg and the vineyards of Domäne Wachau.

stops.name: Dürnstein
stops.quote: Dürnstein : Renowned for the ruins of Dürnstein Castle, where Richard the Lionheart was held captive in the Middle Ages.

stops.name: Dürnstein Castle
stops.quote: Dürnstein : Renowned for the ruins of Dürnstein Castle, where Richard the Lionheart was held captive in the Middle Ages.

stops.name: Weißenkirchen in der Wachau
stops.quote: Weißenkirchen in der Wachau : A wine-growing centre surrounded by terraced vineyards and historic churches.

stops.name: Krems an der Donau
stops.quote: Krems an der Donau : One of Austria’s oldest cities, with a vibrant cultural scene, including museums and festivals.

stops.name: Kunsthalle Krems
stops.quote: Highlights include the Danube Festival in Krems, the Glatt & Verkehrt Festival in Spitz, the Summer Plays in Melk, and the Kunsthalle Krems .
